title: tool-calling: improve execution ergonomics for parallel multi-tool calls, result injection, and retry semantics
author: Morgan Lee
description: Context: Tool-calling ergonomics (multi-tool orchestration, parallel executions, and robust injection of tool outputs back into the LLM context) have surfaced several developer pain points in production: (1) when multiple tools are requested in a single call, tooling around deterministic ordering, result injection, and retries is awkward; (2) parallel tool calls occasionally raced with KV-cache/state updates causing inconsistent injected results in follow-up prompts; (3) retry semantics were too coarse (retries re-run full tool sequences which can be expensive or non-idempotent). Motivation: improve API ergonomics so framework and application authors can express multi-tool workflows with predictable execution ordering, safe parallelism, fine-grained retry controls, and clear structured output for downstream evaluation. This PR implements a set of changes across the API layer, runtime dispatcher, and the OpenAI-compat layer to support: - explicit per-tool call metadata (id, idempotency_hint, run_in_parallel boolean) surfaced in the high-level SDK and in the HTTP JSON payloads; - a deterministic execution planner that groups tools into parallelizable batches while preserving explicit ordering constraints; - lightweight result-injection transactions: tool results are buffered and injected into the LLM input as a single consistent delta after a batch completes to avoid partial-state visibility during parallel execution; - retry policy hooks at the tool-call granularity (max_retries, retry_on_transient, backoff_ms) implemented in the dispatcher; retries re-execute only failed tools in a batch and replay injections deterministically; - improved OpenAI-compatible response format showing tool call events, tool results, and a top-level structured output field for evals and observability; - tests, docs, and migration guidance. Implementation summary: - API: extended the /v1/generate and /v1/chat endpoints to accept an optional "tools" array where each tool object may include id, name, args, run_in_parallel, idempotency_hint, and retry_policy. Backwards compatibility preserved: older calls without tools keep current semantics. - Dispatcher/runtime: introduced Planner and BatchExecutor modules. Planner creates execution batches honoring explicit ordering; BatchExecutor runs parallel tool calls using a controlled worker pool, buffers results, and applies injection transactionally. - Retry semantics: per-tool retry policy implemented with exponential backoff; retries are limited to the scope of a single high-level request and respect idempotency_hint to optionally skip retrying non-idempotent tools. - OpenAI-compat: updated event stream and final response JSON to include tool_call events (tool_call.start, tool_call.result, tool_call.error, tool_call.retry) and a new top-level field "tooling" that lists calls and their final injected output. - Observability: emit structured metrics for tool_call.latency/tool_call.retries/tool_call.success and tracing spans that include tool id and batch id. - Tests: unit tests for planner and executor, integration tests with the example echo-tool and non-idempotent counter-tool, flakiness tests simulating transient failures and slow responses. - Docs: added API examples, migration guidance, and a short explainer for deterministic injection semantics. Rollout plan: feature gated behind interactive flag and disabled by default for hosted customers until we complete a Canary on Dedicated. The flag allows SDKs to opt-in. Checklist: - [x] API schema changes and backwards compat preserved - [x] Planner + BatchExecutor implementation - [x] Per-tool retry policy and idempotency handling - [x] Transactional result injection - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] OpenAI-compat event updates - [x] SDK examples and docs - [x] Observability metrics and tracing - [x] Feature flag gating and migration notes Risks and mitigations: - Non-idempotent tools: added idempotency_hint and default conservative retry behavior (no retries for unknown non-idempotent tools) and clear docs. - Partial visibility during parallel runs: solved by buffering and transactional injection after batch completion. - Increased latency when batching: planner heuristics limit batch size and prefer small parallel groups for low-latency use cases. Related: ENG-4823 (tooling ergonomics), SUP-712 (customer report of inconsistent tool-injected summary).
commits: feat(api): accept 'tools' array on /v1/generate and /v1/chat with per-tool metadata
perf(dispatcher): add Planner to group tools into parallelizable batches
feat(runtime): BatchExecutor executes parallel tool calls and buffers injection
feat(retries): per-tool retry policy with backoff and idempotency checks
chore(tests): add unit/integration tests for planner/executor and retry flows
docs: add API examples and migration guide
fix(ci): adjust integration test timeouts to account for controlled backoff
review_comments: Ava Chen: Can you clarify how we surface partial failures to the caller? Should we return a structured error that lists which tools failed vs succeeded?
Ravi Patel: Nice planner. Two concerns: (1) make sure runtime worker pool size is configurable per deployment; (2) I think the backoff defaults are aggressive for Dedicated low-latency customers.
Diego Alvarez: Please add a test for mixing idempotent and non-idempotent tools in a single batch so we validate retry opt-outs.
Ava Chen: The OpenAI-compat event naming looks good, but ensure old SDKs don't break when seeing unknown event types in the stream.
author_replies: Morgan Lee: We return a final 'tooling' object that enumerates per-tool status; in addition the top-level response includes a structured 'partial_failure' boolean and a 'failed_tools' list when any tool fails. I'll add an example in docs (done).
Morgan Lee: Worker pool size is a feature-flagged config. Defaults are conservative; added flags and docs for Dedicated tuning.
Morgan Lee: Added integration test mixing idempotent + non-idempotent tools (tests/integration/test_mixed_idempotency.py) and included it in CI matrix.
Morgan Lee: OpenAI-compat streams will ignore unknown event types; we added forwards-compatible parsing in the compat layer and documented the event schema versioning.
